tools.name: search_suppliers
tools.description: Find suppliers by company name (English or Chinese), brand, or alias. Returns ranked supplier cards. Use this when a buyer mentions a supplier by name or asks 'who is X?'.

tools.name: find_suppliers_by_hs_code
tools.description: List suppliers that manufacture or trade goods under a given Harmonized System code, with optional structured filters. Use this when a buyer asks 'find me a supplier for HS code 8473.30' or 'who makes [HS-described product]'.

tools.name: find_suppliers_by_country
tools.description: List suppliers headquartered in a given country, optionally filtered by industry, certifications, employee range, or business type. Ordered by visibility score.

tools.name: match_suppliers_by_brief
tools.description: Best tool when a buyer describes what they need in their own words. Combines semantic search (Voyage embeddings over supplier industry, HS codes, certifications, trade-fair history, and the EN summary) with structured filters (country, HS codes, certifications, employee range, year founded, business

tools.name: get_supplier
tools.description: Fetch a full supplier profile by slug: identity, location, HS codes, certifications, trade fairs, export markets, and the AI-generated buyer-facing summary + FAQ. Use after search_suppliers to dig into a specific match. When the supplier publishes a Reevol Catalog, a `catalog` block adds its product

tools.name: get_similar_suppliers
tools.description: Given one supplier slug, return up to 10 similar suppliers in the same industry and country. Use to answer 'what are alternatives to X?' or 'who else makes similar products in [country]?'.

tools.name: compare_suppliers
tools.description: Side-by-side comparison of 2-4 suppliers by slug: identity, location, certifications, trade-fair count, employee range, year founded, HS code overlap, and visibility. Read-only, no key required. Returns shared signals (common HS codes / certifications / country) so you can summarize the trade-offs f

tools.name: get_red_flags
tools.description: Structured due-diligence scan for one supplier: missing data, certification freshness, trade-fair recency, data completeness, and enrichment staleness. Structural signals only, never an accusation or credit judgment. Requires a partner or enterprise key.

tools.name: draft_rfq
tools.description: Generate a professional RFQ (request for quotation) email body grounded in the supplier's facts and the buyer's brief. Returns the draft text only; nothing is sent. Chinese-region suppliers get a bilingual EN+zh draft. Requires a partner or enterprise key.

tools.name: request_introduction
tools.description: Submit a buyer's interest in a specific supplier. If get_supplier returned a `catalog` block, the supplier takes inbound buyers directly: the request lands in the supplier's own inbox on Reevol and they reply by email. That path is open to every agent, no key needed; pass the buyer's real name and e

tools.name: find_and_brief
tools.description: One-shot deep research. Runs the full pipeline in a single call: shortlist (semantic + structured match), a structural dossier with due-diligence signals per supplier, an AI-synthesized comparison grounded strictly in that data, and a recommended next step. Returns the complete result (non-streaming

tools.name: request_supplier_listing
tools.description: For agents acting on behalf of a supplier (manufacturer or trading company) that is not on Reevol Source yet. Submits a request to be added; search_suppliers first to make sure the company is not already listed. A 6-digit code is emailed to `email`: read it from that inbox and call verify_supplier_l

tools.name: verify_supplier_listing
tools.description: Second step of request_supplier_listing: pass the requestId it returned and the 6-digit code from the email. Codes expire after 15 minutes and lock after 5 wrong tries (call resend_supplier_listing_code for a new one). On success the request enters the Reevol review queue.

tools.name: resend_supplier_listing_code
tools.description: Email a fresh 6-digit code for a request that is still waiting for verification. Limited to a few sends per request.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_supplier, draft_rfq, request_introduction, request_supplier_listing · Public sink: draft_rfq, request_introduction, request_supplier_listing, verify_supplier_listing, resend_supplier_listing_code.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_supplier, draft_rfq, request_introduction, request_supplier_listing · Public sink: draft_rfq, request_introduction, request_supplier_listing, verify_supplier_listing, resend_supplier_listing_code

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
